newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil gains no support from firmer crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil gains no support from firmer crude.

text.p: Fuel oil took little comfort from firmer crude on Friday with local factors taking the lead role.

High sulphur barges were knocked down to $112 fob ARA from $115-117 before edging back to $113-114 amid average bunker demand. Cargoes were steady at $110-112 fob NWE unlike prices in the Med were very aggresive selling resulted in $107.25 fob Med being done.
Dealers said Russian straight run material that had been overhanging the market has been thinned, but fresh supplies were expected around Tuesday next week.
No other utility followed yesterday's buyer of M-100 at $119.40 cif Ireland but dealers said it continued to demonstrate cracked remains overshadowed by straight run.

Low sulphur cracked activity was slow in line with slack interest from the main Med buyer. The potential of U.S demand kicking in this week never materialised and prices continued to hover around $122-124 fob NWE. Dealers said suppliers were rolling over cargoes if able to and at least three to four will come available in November. But most were seen to be 30kt or less with only one firm 50kt set to be offered.
